lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: November 22, 1987. Chicago TV got interrupted by someone who has never been caught.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: About 9:14 p.m. A sports segment on one station. The screen goes black for around 15 seconds.

lines.speaker: moth
lines.text: Is it supposed to do that?

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Then a figure appears in a Max Headroom mask and sunglasses, swaying in front of a moving metal panel. No usable sound, only a buzz.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Engineers changed the frequency of the studio link and it stopped. The sports anchor said: "Well, if you're wondering what's happened, so am I."

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: About two hours later, it happened again on a public TV channel, at about 11:20 p.m. This time with sound. It lasted about 90 seconds, and viewers saw an odd, rambling bit of mischief. Nobody on duty could stop it. It ended when the pirates stopped transmitting.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: How? A stronger microwave signal aimed at the stations' towers overrode the real one. It took skill and equipment, and it's very hard to do today.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The FCC investigated and found no culprit. The legal time limit ran out in 1992. Nobody has ever been identified.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: A masked figure took over two TV stations. And walked away.

scenes.visual: TV shows sports segment, goes black
scenes.caption: 15 SECONDS

scenes.visual: Silhouette in a generic mask swaying, buzzing audio
scenes.caption: NO SOUND

scenes.visual: Anchor shrug card with the real quote
scenes.caption: "SO AM I"

scenes.visual: Two towers, a stronger beam overrides
scenes.caption: STRONGER SIGNAL
